title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (Addition of Relevant Enactments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations add to the list of “relevant enactments” for the purposes of sections 13 to 17 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (c. 29) (“the Act”). Under section 13 of the Act, the Treasury may make regulations (an “FMI sandbox”) which may modify the effect or application of such relevant enactments for the purpose of testing the efficiency or effectiveness of new technologies or practices in the carrying on of financial markets infrastructure activities. The effect is to include new relevant enactments within the list at section 17(3) of the Act so that these enactments can be modified by future or existing FMI sandboxes.

title: The Budget (Scotland) Act 2026 Amendment Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Budget (Scotland) Act 2026 (“the Act”).

title: The Education (School Attendance Order) (Wales) Regulations 2026 / Rheoliadau Addysg (Gorchymyn Mynychu’r Ysgol) (Cymru) 2026
summary:
Under section 437(3) of the Education Act 1996 a local authority is required to serve a school attendance order, which is to be in the prescribed form, on the parent of a child of compulsory school age who fails to satisfy the authority that the child is receiving suitable education, and the authority is of the opinion that it is expedient that the child should attend school. These Regulations prescribe the form of a school attendance order to be served by the local authority in Wales for the purposes of section 437(3).

title: The Scottish Languages Act 2025 (Commencement No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring section 6 of the Scottish Languages Act 2025 (“the Act”) into force on 30 November 2026.

title: The Air Departure Tax (Scotland) Act 2017 (Commencement No. 2) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force a number of provisions in Part 2 (key concepts), Part 3 (tax rates) (to the extent that the relevant provisions are not already in force), and Part 4 (payment, collection and management of tax) of the Air Departure Tax (Scotland) Act 2017 (“the Act”) on 1 December 2026. These provisions are required in connection with facilitating the voluntary registration of taxpayers in advance of Air Departure Tax (“ADT”) coming into operation on 1 April 2027 and to enable the Scottish Ministers to make regulations concerning tax bands and tax rate amounts for ADT.

title: Act of Adjournal (Criminal Procedure Rules 1996 Amendment) (Criminal Justice Modernisation and Abusive Domestic Behaviour Reviews (Scotland) Act 2025) 2026
summary: This Act of Adjournal makes various amendments to the Criminal Procedure Rules 1996 (“the 1996 Rules”) in connection with the Criminal Justice Modernisation and Abusive Domestic Behaviour Reviews (Scotland) Act 2025 (“the 2025 Act”).

title: The Circular Economy (Scotland) Act 2024 (Commencement No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring provisions of the Circular Economy (Scotland) Act 2024 (“the Act”) into force.

title: The Hemp (Third Country Imports) (Amendment) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under section 11 of, paragraph 11M of Part 1C of Schedule 2 to, the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. The EU provisions relating to the import of hemp from third countries are set out in Regulation (EU)  1308/2013 which is directly applicable in Northern Ireland under Article 5(4) of, and Annex 2 to, the Windsor Framework. These Regulations amend the Hemp (Third Country Import) Regulations 2002 (S.I. 2002/787) as they apply in Northern Ireland in relation to third country imports.

title: The Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 (Commencement No. 5 and Transitional Provisions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force two provisions in the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 (“the 2025 Act”). Regulation 2 brings into force sections 40(3) and 43 on 20th November 2026. Both provisions make amendments to the Transport and Works Act 1992. Regulation 3 makes transitional provision. It provides that section 40(3) applies to applications under section 1 or 3 of the Transport and Works Act 1992 made before these Regulations came into force only where a relevant notice has not yet been issued in respect of that application. The amendments made by section 43 do not apply to applications made before these Regulations come into force.

title: The Social Security (Non-Benefit Payments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify which payments are a “non-benefit payment” under section 121DA(5) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992 (c. 5) (“the Administration Act”).

title: The Value Added Tax (Distance Selling) (Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend Schedules 9ZD, 9ZE and Part 3 of Schedule 9ZF to the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and come into force on 1st January 2027. They implement certain amendments made by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 to Council Directive 2006/112/EC (“the VAT Directive”), pursuant to the United Kingdom’s obligations under the Windsor Framework.

title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Specified Area) (Restricted Area EGR160) Regulations 2026
The Government Resources and Accounts (Northern Ireland) Act 2001 (Estimates and Accounts) (Designation of Bodies) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Government Resources and Accounts (Northern Ireland) Act 2001 (Estimates and Accounts) (Designation of Bodies) Order 2026 (S.I. 2026 No. 49) (“the principal Order”), which designates specified central government bodies in relation to named government departments for the purpose of those departments’ supply estimates and resource accounts.

title: The Online Safety Act 2023 (Commencement No. 8) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are the eighth commencement regulations made under the Online Safety Act 2023 (c. 50) (“the Act”). They bring into force section 75 of the Act which places duties on providers of Category 1, 2A and 2B services to set out their policies on disclosing information to the parents of deceased child users, have a dedicated helpline or section of the service (or similar means) for such parents, provide details about the relevant policies and procedures in their terms of service or a publicly available statement, and respond in a timely manner to requests for information. Section 75 also requires the providers to operate a complaints procedure in relation to these duties.

title: The Rehabilitation of Offenders (Exceptions) (Amendment No. 2) Order (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: This Order amends the Rehabilitation of Offenders (Exceptions) Order (Northern Ireland) 1979 (“the 1979 Order”) to bring individuals who are seeking to assess children and vulnerable adults as registered health care professionals employed or engaged by the Department for Communities, or by its contractors or sub-contractors, who are carrying out activities for the Department for Communities, within the excluded circumstances set out in Article 2 of the 1979 Order.

title: The Police Act 1997 (Criminal Records) (Amendment No. 2) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Police Act 1997 (Criminal Records) (Disclosure) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2008 (“the 2008 Regulations”) to make provision for enhanced criminal record checks with suitability information in relation to individuals who are seeking to assess children and vulnerable adults as registered Health Care Professionals employed or engaged by the Department for Communities, or by its contractors or sub-contractors, who are carrying out activities for the Department for Communities.

title: The Railways (Interoperability in Northern Ireland) (Convention on International Carriage by Rail) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations implement Directive (EU) 2016/797 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on the interoperability of the rail system within the European Union (O.J. No. L 138, 26.5.2016, p. 44) (the “2016 Directive”) for Northern Ireland, making technical provision for the placing on the market, putting into service and free movement of railway products. The 2016 Directive is a recast of Directive 2008/57/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2008 (O.J. No. L 191, 18.7.2008, p. 1), which was transposed for Great Britain and Northern Ireland by way of the Railways (Interoperability) Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/3066). These Regulations replace that regime for Northern Ireland in line with the UK’s obligations pursuant to Article 5(4) and Annex II of the Windsor Framework.

title: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate BlackRock Financial Management, Inc., Bloomberg L.P., Bottomline Technologies Limited, Broadridge Financial Solutions Limited and Form3 UK Limited as critical third parties. The Regulations amend the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/777) to add the entities to the list of designated critical third parties.

title: The Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Human Rights Act 1998 (“the HRA”) to address a finding of the European Court of Human Rights of a breach of Article 13 of the European Convention on Human Rights (“the Convention”) in the case of S.W. v United Kingdom (Application no. 87/18).
